peopleAlsoAsk.snippet: Storage and Transportation of Vaccines Vaccines must be stored in a dedicated refrigerator maintained at a temperature range of 2-8°C (35-46°F). It is critical to use a min/max thermometer to regularly monitor and verify the temperature.

peopleAlsoAsk.question: Can chickens survive Newcastle disease?
peopleAlsoAsk.snippet: Previously known as velogenic viscerotropic Newcastle disease, END is one of the most infectious diseases of poultry in the world. The mortality in unvaccinated birds can reach 100 percent, and birds may die without any clinical signs of disease.

peopleAlsoAsk.question: Is OPV heat or freeze sensitive?
peopleAlsoAsk.snippet: The Oral Polio Vaccine (OPV) is the most heat sensitive vaccine, meaning it rapidly loses effectiveness when exposed to higher temperatures. Due to this sensitivity, OPV requires storage at very low temperatures (around -20°C) and strict maintenance of the cold chain.

peopleAlsoAsk.question: What is the thermal stability of Newcastle disease virus in poultry litter?
peopleAlsoAsk.snippet: At high temperatures (37.8 C-43.3 C), infectious virus could not be detected after 2-7 days, whereas at lower temperatures (10 C-21.1 C), it took up to 112 days for virus to decrease to undetectable levels. Furthermore, the D values were almost always shorter in the high moisture litter.Apr 5, 2022
